title: Integrated communication: Philosophy — schools of ethics

frames.title: Lesson 130 · Integrated communication: Philosophy — schools of ethics

body: **Foco:** Comunicação integrada: Filosofia.
**Pronúncia:** Ritmo e ênfase para nuances.
**24 palavras novas** (filosofia).
**Texto do dia:** infográfico em texto.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre as principais escolas de ética a partir de um infográfico em texto, comparando e sintetizando posições.

body: Esta aula treina **escrever frases claras e corretas (IELTS Writing, TOEFL Writing)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Five Ways of Asking “What Should I Do?”
items: Judge actions by **outcomes**: the best act **maximizes good**.
Judge by **duties and rules**: some acts are **wrong whatever the result**.
Ask what a **person of good character** would do.
Act on principles **nobody could reasonably reject**.
Stress **relationships** and **responsibility** to those who depend on us.
blocks.note: Simplified overview; each school has many versions and critics.

items.q: Deontology judges acts only by results.
items.why: duties and rules; wrong whatever the result.

items.q: The infographic claims each school has one fixed version.

head: Estrutura
Exemplo
Nota
rows: Deontology stresses duties, **whereas** consequentialism stresses outcomes.
responsibility to **those who** depend on us

blocks.body: Ao **comparar** escolas filosóficas, use **whereas/while**, **whatever** e relativas sem *that*: *principles (that) nobody could reject*.
*Moral* e *ethical* são quase sinônimos no uso comum; em filosofia, *ethics* é o estudo, *morality* é o código.

items.s: Some acts are wrong ___ the result. (whatever)
Deontology stresses duties, ___ consequentialism stresses outcomes. (whereas)
Care ethics stresses responsibility to those ___ depend on us. (who)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.ans: By the rule whatever the result

body: **Weigh the options** — pesar as opções
**Do the right thing** — fazer a coisa certa
**The end justifies the means** — os fins justificam os meios
**Moral high ground** — superioridade moral
**Gray area** — área cinzenta
**Lesser of two evils** — o menor de dois males
**Let one’s conscience be one’s guide** — seguir a consciência
**Sit on the fence** — ficar em cima do muro
**Cross the Rubicon** — passar do ponto sem volta
**Black and white** — preto no branco
**How would a deontologist judge that act?** — Como um deontologista julgaria esse ato?
**By the rule, whatever the result.** — Pela regra, independentemente do resultado.
**And a consequentialist?** — E um consequencialista?

blocks.title: Seminar
lines: How would a deontologist judge that act?
Como um deontologista julgaria esse ato?
By the rule, whatever the result.
By outcomes, whereas virtue ethics asks about character.
Pelos resultados, ao passo que a ética das virtudes pergunta sobre o caráter.

blocks.title: Pronúncia: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances

items.label: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances
items.note: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances: o acento muda o sentido (He said she STOLE it × he said SHE stole it) e as pausas separam ideias técnicas densas.
words: I didn’t SAY he did it.
I didn’t say HE did it.
I didn’t say he DID it.

prompts.model: Deontology stresses duties, whereas consequentialism stresses outcomes.
Lying is wrong, whatever the result, say some deontologists.
It asks what a person of good character would do.

blocks.task: Write a text infographic (5 items) comparing schools of ethics, using whereas and whatever.
blocks.model: Consequentialism: judge by outcomes. Deontology: judge by duties, whatever the result. Virtue ethics: ask about character, whereas the first two ask about acts. Contractualism: act on principles nobody could reject. Care ethics: stress responsibility to those who depend on us.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
